problem.text: A rectangle is partitioned into $5$ regions as shown. Each region is to be painted a solid color—red, orange, yellow, blue, or green—so that regions that touch are painted different colors, and colors can be used more than once. How many different colorings are possible?

steps.title: Where to start: color the most crowded regions first
steps.body: In coloring problems, start with the regions that have the most neighbors, because they have the most rules to follow. Call the regions top-left (TL), top-right (TR), bottom-left (BL), bottom-middle (BM) and bottom-right (BR). Look for a group of regions that all touch each other.

your_turn.prompt: Which three regions all touch one another?
your_turn.answer: TL, TR and BM: TL touches TR, and both top regions sit above part of BM.

steps.title: Color the three that touch
steps.body: TL, TR and BM must get three different colors. Pick them one at a time: TL has $5$ choices, TR has $4$, and BM has $3$. That gives $5\cdot 4\cdot 3 = 60$ ways.

your_turn.prompt: Why does BM have exactly $3$ choices, and not $4$?
your_turn.answer: BM touches both TL and TR, which already use two different colors, so $5-2 = 3$ colors are left.

steps.title: Add the two outer regions
steps.body: BL touches only TL and BM. Those two already have different colors, so BL has $5-2 = 3$ choices. Careful: BL does not touch TR or BR, so do not rule out their colors too.

your_turn.prompt: How many choices does BR have? Which regions does it touch?
your_turn.answer: $3$ choices. BR touches only TR and BM, which have different colors.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Multiply the choices: $$60\cdot 3\cdot 3 = 540.$$ Another way: color BM first ($5$ ways), then go along BL, TL, TR, BR, where each region must avoid BM and the one before it: $4\cdot 3\cdot 3\cdot 3 = 108$, and $5\cdot 108 = 540$. The answer is **(D)** $540$.

wrong_choices.A: This is $5! = 120$, which counts colorings where all five regions get different colors. But colors can be reused on regions that do not touch, such as BL and BR.
wrong_choices.E: This comes from missing that BR touches TR, so BR gets $4$ choices instead of $3$: $60\cdot 3\cdot 4 = 720$. Check the figure: the top-right region sits above BR.
